Subject: Helios capacity ask: tri-region safety buffer and trigger points

Hi Lauren,

Thanks again for the demo last week. The exec team at Helios liked the predictability promises, and procurement asked me to get a concrete ask in writing so we can coordinate SOW and internal approvals. High level: they want a committed pool that covers steady-state inference for the next 12 months plus a buffer for two planned product launches in Q3/Q4.

Numbers they shared (approx):
- Steady state: ~120 concurrent tokens/sec across inference pipelines (mostly chat gen + embeddings)
- Peak launch multiplier: x3 sustained for 72 hours, occasional x6 bursts for short windows

We need: recommended pool sizing (per region US/EU/APAC), suggested reserved-node buffer for deal triggers, and a short runbook for failover (if APAC capacity is constrained, route to EU with <50ms added lat target). Can you send a slide or sheet we can give procurement?

Alice
Head of Platform Partnerships
Helios AI

Hi Alice —

Appreciate the clear ask. I've attached a preliminary workbook (Q2_capacity_slate.xlsx) with per-region node counts, a conservative safety buffer, and the deal-trigger matrix we recommend for CLI-3842. Quick summary up-front:

- Recommended baseline pools: US 40 nodes, EU 30 nodes, APAC 25 nodes (nodes sized for M-class GPUs; exact mix in sheet).
- Safety buffer: +20% reserved pool across each region, plus a 10-node global surge lane that can be routed to any region with 1-hour activation.
- Triggers: automated thresholds at 70% sustained utilization for 6 hours (auto-notify), 85% for 30 minutes (apply buffer), and 95% (manual escalation to infra ops + 24h immediate reserve).

I've cc'd Karthik and Ben to weigh in on regional constraints and procurement language. If procurement needs a minimal SOW paragraph we can provide redlines quickly.

Warmly,
Lauren Bishop
Eng. Lead, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Q2_capacity_slate.xlsx

Thanks — I reviewed the workbook. A few operational notes to make the recommendation more robust for Helios' usage profile:

1) APAC headroom: APAC availability in our Singapore cluster is currently tighter in mid-July due to another onboarding; we should either: a) shift 5 nodes from APAC buffer into the global surge lane and guarantee 2-week activation lead time for permanent capacity, or b) offer a cross-region failover SLA (route to EU with weighted latency budget).

2) Node sizing: Helios' mix suggests heavy decoding (chat flows). Move 30% of baseline M-class nodes to L-class (latency-optimized) in US and EU to keep 99th percentile latency below 120ms on steady state. Sheet updated in tab 'NodeMix_v2'.

3) Billing/commit terms: propose a 12-month reserved commitment for baseline, with a 3-month rolling clause for surge credits (unused surge capacity converts to credits applied quarterly). Procurement will want exact language — suggest we prepare the paragraph and include in the SOW redline.

If we agree, I'll draft the SOW paragraph and an activation playbook. Ben — can you confirm the activation playbook steps (obs + ASGs + manual approval chain)?

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Architect

Looping in a brief activation checklist below and confirming attachments (SOW redline attached).

Activation checklist (short form):
- Pre-activation: verify quota & node images, confirm KMS keys for Helios tenant, provision network routes in target region. (Infra lead: Ben)
- T-60m: raise runbook, enable traffic mirroring for 10% of sessions for latency verification. (Ops)
- T-30m: enable surge lane routing and auto-scale policy at 2x baseline. Monitor 95th p90 latency and token throughput. (SRE + CS)
- Escalation: if latency >150ms for 15m, route to fallback model in EU; if throughput drops >20%, auto-warm additional nodes and notify Lauren/Karthik.

Activation of the global surge lane requires written notice and may incur an activation lead time of up to 14 days for permanent capacity resizes; temporary surge activation will be executed per the agreed activation playbook included as Appendix A."
